default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Sato is a very kind person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks Mr. Sato as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies 親切な and shows a very high degree of kindness.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 親切 is a な adjective, so な is used to connect it to the noun 人.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 人 is the main noun modified by 親切な, while です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: は makes the person being discussed the topic. とても adds degree to 親切, and because 親切 is a な adjective placed before 人, な is needed to connect it to the noun.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: With an い adjective, connect it directly to the noun, such as 優しい人, without adding な.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な after the adjective な when placing the adjective before a noun.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: Recently, hot days have continued, but today is especially hot.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ AいN が ＋ Vている が、 ＋ N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ Aい
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん indicates the time or period when an event occurs.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks あつい日 as the subject of the continuing event.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ている shows a continuing state, while が connects the previous clause to the contrasting idea that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: は shifts the topic to today for comparison with recent days.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 特別 modifies あつい and emphasizes that today is unusually hot.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: あつい is the main predicate and describes today's condition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: さいきん gives the time background, after which あつい日がつづいている describes a continuing situation. が creates a contrast, and then 今日 は is made the topic to say that today's heat stands out more.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 特別 is replaced with とても, the sentence only says that today is very hot. It does not necessarily suggest that it is unusually hot compared with other days.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate が as “and,” but in this sentence が expresses the contrasting meaning “but.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: Do you have any plans for the summer vacation?
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the noun “summer vacation” to modify the noun “plans” that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes “plans” the main topic being asked about in the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word 何 combines with the particle か to form an indefinite pronoun meaning “something” or “anything.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The existential predicate あります combines with the particle か at the end of the sentence to form a question.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The sentence makes “summer vacation plans” the topic with the particle は. It then uses the indefinite expression 何か with the interrogative predicate ありますか to politely ask whether any plans exist.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This asks directly about a specific action, “What will you do?” rather than asking whether the other person has any plans.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 何か (is there anything?—a yes-or-no question) with 何を (what will you do?—a question asking for specific information).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: I often walk through this park on my way home.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies “I” as the topic and subject of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The frequency adverb modifies the sequence of walking through the park and then going home.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を is used with movement verbs to indicate the space that the action passes through.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 通る takes the て form to connect the sequence of movements.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に marks the final destination and combines with the verb かえります for going home.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the frequency adverb, the phrase showing the space passed through (を), connected by the て form to show a sequence of actions, and ending with the destination (に) and the main verb.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle で describes where a specific action takes place inside the park, such as jogging or playing, rather than movement through it as with を.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often mistakenly use the particle で instead of を before movement verbs that pass through a space, such as 通る, 渡る, and 散歩する.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: My younger brother is interested in world news.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the younger brother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun “world” to modify the noun “news” that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the target of an emotion or interest.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the verb 持つ.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 持つ takes the ている form to express a continuously maintained mental state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The sentence uses the fixed phrase “～に興味を持つ.” The object of interest takes the particle に, while the continuing mental state is expressed with the ている form.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Both express interest, but 興味がある describes an objective state, while 興味を持つ emphasizes the subject's deliberate interest.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle を or で instead of に when expressing “be interested in something.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.tokens.9.m: be, be in the process of
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.cn: N ＋ に興味がある・に興味を持つ
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: I am learning about Japan's industry.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the noun “Japan” to modify the noun “industry” that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The grammar pattern について follows a noun to indicate the topic or subject being studied or researched.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 調べる takes the ています form to show that the action of looking up or learning about something is in progress.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The sentence omits the subject “I” and uses the structure ～について directly after the noun phrase to state the research topic before the progressive predicate しらべています.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses an attitude or action directed straight at an object, and is not used to state a research topic like について.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: When using について to modify a noun directly after it, learners often forget to change it to についての.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: What should I prepare for tomorrow's party?
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the time expression for the noun “party” that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the purpose and combines with the particle は to emphasize the party setting as the topic.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word 何 combines with the object particle を to mark what needs to be prepared.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 用意する takes the conditional ば form as the basis for asking for advice.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The sentence-ending pattern ～ばいいですか is used to ask the listener for advice or guidance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The context topic is placed first with には. Then the question word 何 serves as the object (を) of the verb in the conditional form, combined with the advice-seeking pattern ～ばいいですか.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This asks whether one should prepare something or not, requiring a yes-or-no choice, instead of asking openly for specific instructions about what dish to prepare, as in ～ばいいですか.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Be careful to use the correct conditional forms (ば/たら) of the verb when combining it with the advice-seeking pattern ～ばいいですか.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.cn: Vば・Vたら・Vと + いいですか
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: If it rains, the concert will be canceled.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of a natural phenomenon in a conditional subordinate clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb ふる uses the たら form to express the conditional assumption “if... then...”.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the concert the main topic of the result clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate expresses the action or decision that will be carried out when the condition occurs.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: This compound sentence places the conditional clause using the たら form first, followed by the main clause, which states the topic and the corresponding decision.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: The pattern と expresses an inevitable natural result, so it is less suitable than たら when the following clause expresses a deliberate human decision.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use と instead of たら in sentences where the following clause expresses intention, a decision, or a suggestion.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.cn: Vた・Aかった・Aな/Nだった + ら
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: My older sister is 17 years old this year.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The modifier comes before and describes the following noun for a family member.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the topic introduced in the sentence as the older sister.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate confirms the topic’s age using a number expression with です.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The sentence uses the basic information pattern「A は B です」to state the older sister’s age; the noun phrase「わたしの姉」is made the main topic by the particle「は」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Used to address or refer politely to another person’s older sister. It is not used for one’s own older sister when speaking to outsiders.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: When introducing a family member from your own family to outsiders, use「姉」instead of「お姉さん」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I always buy the same kind of bread.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that an action happens continuously or regularly.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The word directly modifies the following noun, bread, without using a particle.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を identifies bread as the object affected by the action of buying.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb functions as the predicate and expresses the action of buying.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The word「おなじ」has the special grammatical feature of combining directly with the noun「パン」to modify it; the particle「を」marks the object chosen for purchase.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because when「同じ」comes before a noun to modify it, it does not take the particle「の」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This is grammatically incorrect because「同じ」does not use the ending「な」when directly modifying the following noun.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: Do not add「の」or「な」after「同じ」when it directly modifies a noun immediately after it.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative placed before a noun to identify a specific seat near the speaker.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the seat the topic being asked about.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb in the て form combines with います to express the vacant state of something, together with the question particle か.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: V（ intransitive verb ）て + います
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The verb「空く」is an intransitive verb showing a change of state. When changed to the「〜ています」form, it shows that the resulting state continues, meaning that the seat is still vacant, rather than showing an action in progress.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the transitive verb「開ける」to ask whether the other person intentionally opens something, such as a door or a lid.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Use the intransitive verb「あく」with「〜ています」to ask about whether a seat is vacant. Do not use the transitive verb「あける」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the destination or specific location where the result of the writing will remain.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the address as the object directly affected by the action of writing.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request or instruction.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The sentence makes a polite request using the pattern「〜てください」; because the writing leaves a result on a specific surface or in a specific field, the location receiving the result takes the particle「に」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle「で」emphasizes the place where the writing takes place, such as this room or this desk, rather than the location of the field where the content should be entered.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: When asking someone to fill in or write information in a specific place on paper or a screen, use the particle「に」, which indicates the destination of the result, instead of「で」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: The high school is far from my house.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the starting point or spatial reference point used to measure distance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the high school the main topic for the comment about distance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い combines with です as a polite predicate describing distance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The sentence places the reference point 「わたしのいえから」 first, puts the topic being described 「高校は」 in the middle, and ends with the adjective predicate 「とおい」 to clearly state the quality of the distance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning changes to “the high school is near my house” instead of far.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Be careful not to reverse the positions of から and は, or the topic being described in the sentence will change.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: It is already late, so let’s get ready to leave.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that time has moved into a later stage.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjunction ので connects an objective reason clause to the action that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb directly modifies the noun したく.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action しましょう.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb ending 〜ましょう is used to invite or suggest that the listener do the action together.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The first clause gives an objective reason using the conjunction 「ので」. The second clause uses the modifying clause 「かえるしたく」 as the object of the invitation 「しましょう」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The cause has a more subjective and definite tone than ので.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It is more formal, while したく is commonly used for daily preparations such as eating, drinking, or going out.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: When connecting a noun or an adjective ending in な with ので, you must add な (N なので). Do not forget な and connect them directly.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nな + ので
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: Because this bag is very easy to use, I have continued using it for more than five years now.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は puts the object at the beginning of the sentence as the topic for the explanation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the adjective つかいやすい.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is easy to use,
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern やすい shows ease and combines with the conjunction ので to give an objective reason.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb emphasizing an impressively long period of time.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The suffix いじょう comes after the quantity ５年 to express five years or more.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern つづける combines with the ending ています to show that an action has continued from the past until now.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The sentence uses ので to connect the reason, that the bag is easy to use, with the result, using it for a long time. It combines with the ending 〜つづけています to emphasize that the action of using it has continued for more than five years.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つかっていきます, the action would point toward the future, meaning that it will continue to be used, so it would not express the process maintained over the past five years.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with つかいはじめました, the sentence would only describe the starting point of the action, meaning that one began using it, and would lose the meaning of lasting continuation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Learners should note that the ending 〜つづける attaches directly to the ます form of the verb, with ます removed, rather than connecting through the て form.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: The clothing counter is on the second floor, so please use the escalator over there.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the location of the counter the topic of the announcement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where something exists and is used with the verb ございます.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is located at..., so
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The formal honorific form of あります combines with the conjunction ので to explain the reason.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: This polite direction word combines with the particle の to modify the noun “escalator.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of using.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The honorific pattern ご〜ください is used to make a polite request or give polite instructions to customers.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: お ＋ V(stem) / ご ＋ N(group 3) ＋ ください
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: This is a standard customer-service sentence: the first part uses the high-level polite form 「ございますので」 to state the location, and the second part uses the formal request pattern 「ご〜ください」 to give directions.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This is an ordinary imperative sentence, so it is not formal or polite enough for customer service.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the ordinary polite form, which is less respectful than the honorific ございますので.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: With a two-character Sino-Japanese noun such as 利用, the honorific request form must use the prefix ご (ごりようください), not お.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: Recently, the computer had been running poorly, and in the end it broke down.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This time adverb sets the point in time when the problem occurred.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun “computer” to the noun ぐあい that it modifies.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the following adjective that expresses a state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective いい takes the negative past form and combines with が to connect the earlier situation to the later outcome.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb describes an unwanted outcome that occurs after a long process of change.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The past form of the pattern 〜てしまう expresses that an unfortunate, unintended event has completely happened.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: The first part uses the conjunction 「が」 to describe a long period of trouble. The second part uses the adverb 「とうとう」 and the regret pattern 「〜てしまった」 to show the unavoidable bad result.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This describes an expected good result after a long period of effort, so it is not used for negative results such as breakdowns.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This also means “finally,” but it can be used for both good and bad results and sounds more formal and written.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use the adverb やっと for negative results or breakdowns; in the context of a computer breaking down, use とうとう.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: A: “I heard that you were ill, but you look healthy.” - B: “Yes. Thank goodness, I am well.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.vi: A: “I heard that you were ill
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と quotes information that the speaker received indirectly.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 聞く takes the polite form and combines with が to introduce a direct comment.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The suffix そうだ is attached to an adjective to make a judgment based on appearance, while ね seeks agreement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: This interjection politely confirms something in conversation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: This fixed reply expresses thanks for the other person’s concern.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: Speaker A uses the quotation particle 「〜と聞きました」 with the conjunction 「が」 to begin the conversation, then uses 「〜そう」 to comment on the person’s appearance. Speaker B replies with the standard expression of thanks 「おかげさまで」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This directly states that the other person is healthy, while おげんきそう expresses a judgment based on appearance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This expresses a judgment based on overall observation or indirect information and is less directly visual or emotional than そう.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in な is attached to the appearance-judgment pattern そうだ, な (おげんきそう) must be removed; おげんきなそう must not be kept.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: I can eat anything except beef.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the speaker the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun 以外 combines with the particle は to emphasize the single exception that is excluded.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word combines with でも to express the meaning of all things without exception.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 食べる takes the potential form (可能形) to express the subject’s ability to eat.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The topic 「わたしは」 comes first, followed by the exclusion phrase 「ぎゅうにくいがいは」, which limits the object. This combines with the all-inclusive phrase 「何でも」 and the potential-form verb 「食べられます」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This expresses the limitation “only,” which is the complete opposite of 以外, meaning “except.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: With a group 2 verb such as 食べる, the potential form must be 食べられる. Avoid shortening it to 食べれる in an exam.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: N / V普通形 ＋ 以外（は・に）
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: I thought meeting Tanaka had happened recently, but it was already a year ago.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of the action of meeting.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 会った is nominalized with the particle の and combines with は to become the topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と introduces the content of the thought before おもっていた.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern のに expresses the contrast between a subjective thought and objective reality.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb emphasizes how quickly time has passed.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle も follows a quantity word to emphasize that more time has passed than expected.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: This affirmative predicate states the actual time point when the event occurred.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The sentence uses the conjunction のに to connect a subjective thought with objective reality, expressing surprise and regret that time has passed so quickly.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced with ので, the sentence would show a cause-and-effect relationship and completely lose its contrast and sense of surprise.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with ても, the sentence would express a hypothetical concession and could not describe a fact that has already happened.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Learners must clearly distinguish のに, which shows surprise and regret that go against reality, from ので, which only shows an objective cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or other polite title
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.tokens.14.m: as many as, as much as
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: This coffee is really bitter, isn’t it? Let’s add a little more sugar.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun is placed at the beginning of the sentence with a comma to state the topic of the conversation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.vi: It is quite bitter, isn't it?
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective predicate combines with the ending ね to seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb phrase showing a small amount, modifying the action of adding sugar.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of putting something in.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.vi: Let's put some in, shall we?
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the ましょう form expresses an invitation or suggestion for two people to do something together.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The first sentence uses ずいぶん with the ending ね to comment on the bitterness and seek agreement, while the next sentence continues with the ending ましょう to make a reasonable suggestion for solving the problem.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 入れてください, the sentence becomes a request for the other person to do something and loses the meaning of doing it together expressed by ましょう.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 入れませんか, the sentence sounds more like a polite invitation to ask for the other person's opinion than a direct suggestion.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Learners should be careful not to confuse the invitation ending ましょう (let's...) with the request ending てください (please...).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: This piece of clothing was made in Japan.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun showing origin combines with です to form an affirmative predicate.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: This simple affirmative noun sentence uses the suffix せい (製), attached directly after the country name to show where the product was made.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 日本で作られた is used, the sentence is expressed in a longer passive form, while にほんせい is a short and natural noun expression for showing origin.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Learners should note that the suffix せい is attached directly after the country name, without adding the particle の between them.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: This is the first time I have come here, but I feel safe because a friend is coming to pick me up.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that an action is happening for the first time, modifying the action of going to a place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb directly modifies the noun ばしょ before it.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が connects the two clauses with a mild contrast between feeling unfamiliar and feeling safe.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of coming to pick someone up.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the ます form drops ます and combines with the particle に to show the purpose of movement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.vi: because someone comes to pick me up
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern てくれる shows gratitude for an action that benefits the speaker, and combines with から to state the reason.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective ending な combines with です to form a predicate showing a comfortable and relieved mental state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The first clause gives the worrying situation (coming here for the first time) and connects with が. The second clause uses the pattern 〜てくれる together with から to clearly show that the reason for feeling safe is that a friend is coming to pick the speaker up.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 来てあげる, the direction of the action changes to the speaker doing something for the friend, so the meaning of the sentence becomes completely wrong.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来てもらう is used, the person receiving the favor is me, used with は/が, while the friend is used with に (友だちに来てもらう). This differs from てくれる, where the doer (友だち) is used with が.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle used with the person performing the action in てくれる (the person who does が does it for me) and てもらう (I ask someone to do に).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects a time noun to modify the noun テスト.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the topic being commented on or evaluated in the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending な combines with でした to form an affirmative predicate describing a past state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: This simple statement uses the particle の to identify when the test took place, the particle は to state the topic, and the ending でした to comment on the nature of an event that ended in the past.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If やさしかったです is used, the sentence has the same meaning but uses the past form of the adjective ending い instead of the adjective ending な.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Learners should remember that the past form of the adjective ending な is でした, and avoid incorrectly changing it to the ending い, such as かんたんかったです.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: I bought a ring at the department store.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.sk: N(place) で + N(thing) を + Vました
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place where the shopping action takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action 買いました.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past form (ました).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The sentence describes an action that took place in the past at a specific location. The structure consists of a place with the particle 「で」, an object with the particle 「を」, and a verb ending in the polite past form 「〜ました」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the particle に is used, it shows existence or the destination of movement, not the place where a buying or selling action takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: The distinction is important: use で (デパートで買う) for where an action takes place, but use に (デパートにある) for where an object exists.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective ending い in its basic form directly modifies the noun きって that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of receiving (もらいました).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate describes the action of receiving and is in the polite past form (ました).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: The noun phrase 「めずらしいきって」 consists of the adjective ending い directly modifying the noun. It functions as the object marked by the particle 「を」 of the receiving verb 「もらいました」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あげました, the meaning changes to 'I gave the rare stamp to someone' instead of 'I received it.'
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれました is used, the subject must be another person giving something to me, while with もらいました, the implied subject is 'I' (the receiver).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: When もらいました is used, the implied subject is always the receiver, usually 'I,' unlike くれました, where the subject is the giver.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: No matter how cheap something is, I do not buy it if I do not need it.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb used with the concessive pattern 〜ても to emphasize the degree.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: no matter how cheap it is
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 安い changes its ending to くても to express a concessive condition (even if it is cheap).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the short negative form (ない) directly modifies the noun もの that follows.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the object phrase the topic to emphasize the negative attitude in the following clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.vi: I will not buy it either.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is in the polite negative form (ません), showing a firm decision.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: This pattern combines the adverb 「いくら」 with the form 「〜ても」 to emphasize a hypothetical concessive condition to a high degree. The second clause uses the particle 「は」 to state the topic 'things that are not needed,' together with the firm negative predicate 「買いません」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 〜ば (安ければ) is used, it means the favorable condition 'if it is cheap,' which is completely different from the concessive meaning of 〜ても.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 〜のに is used, it describes something that actually happened together with regret or surprise ('it was cheap, but I did not buy it'), rather than the hypothetical principle expressed by 〜ても.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: When changing the adjective ending い to the concessive form 〜ても, change the ending い to くても (安くても), and do not confuse it with 安いでも.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.cn: いくら + Vても・Aいくても・Aなでも・Nでも
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: After I come home from school, I will prepare for the lesson in advance.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から shows the starting point of the action of returning.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the た form combines with ら to show that an action happens after the previous action is completed.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb します.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate is in the polite affirmative form (ます), expressing a future intention.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The structure 「Vたら」 connects two actions in a clear future time sequence (after finishing V1, V2 will be done). The starting point uses the particle 「から」, and the following action is 「よしゅうをします」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 〜と is used, it has the meaning of a habit or natural law, so the following clause is unnatural with a personal intentional action such as します.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 〜ば is used, it mainly expresses the simple hypothetical condition 'if I return' and does not clearly show the order of finishing the first action before doing the next one as 〜たら does.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: When the pattern 「〜たら」 expresses a time sequence (after finishing A, do B), the verb must be changed to the past form (た) before adding ら.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The stem of a group 2 verb つかれる.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjugated ending of a group 2 verb in the dictionary form.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: A group 2 verb (一段動詞) in the dictionary form, used to show that the body or mind becomes less energetic after a lot of work or activity.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: When つかれた (the past form) is used, it describes the state of being tired at the moment of speaking in everyday conversation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: In everyday speech, Japanese people usually use the past form 「つかれた」 to say “I am tired,” rather than the dictionary form 「つかれる」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The stem of the -i adjective はずかしい (恥ずかしい).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The basic ending of an -i adjective, showing a shy or embarrassed emotional state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: はずかしい (恥ずかしい) is an -i adjective that describes the speaker’s shy, confused, or embarrassed feelings toward other people in a specific situation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: はずかしがる is a verb used to describe a third person’s shy or embarrassed behavior. It is not used for the speaker’s own direct feelings.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: When describing another person’s embarrassment (third person), you must change to はずかしがる or はずかしがっている instead of using はずかしい directly.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi:
(On a train)
A: “The train is emptier than I expected.”
B: “That’s right. It’s good that we could get seats.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase showing the setting where the conversation takes place, with the particle で.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A comparison phrase with a past-tense verb + より, meaning “more than originally expected.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb すく in the ている form describes an uncrowded state, together with the sentence-ending particle ね.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A phrase showing agreement with the other speaker’s opinion.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 座る is changed into the potential form and then into the て form to act as the reason clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜てよかった expresses relief or happiness because the result was good.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: A uses “思ったより” to compare the actual emptiness with the original expectation. B uses the verb 座る in the potential form, changed into the て form (座れて/すわれて), followed by the pattern “よかった” to express happiness about getting a seat on the train.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 〜ばよかった shows regret about not doing something in the past. This is opposite to 〜てよかった, which shows that one feels lucky because something good happened.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 〜てはいけない is used to forbid an action. It is not used to express happiness like 〜てよかった.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 〜てよかった (it was lucky that something was done or happened) with 〜ばよかった (if only I had done it—regret about missing the chance).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aで・Nで ＋ よかった
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi:
(In front of the station)
A: “I’m sorry I ended up being late.”
B: “No, it’s all right. I also just arrived.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place and setting where the conversation takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.vi: A: “Because I ended up being late
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the てしまって form describes something that happened unintentionally and forms a reason clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: A polite predicate used to apologize to the other person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: An interjection used in response to an apology.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: A reassuring predicate phrase combined with the sentence-ending particle よ to give the listener new information.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle も shows similarity and helps reduce the other person’s feeling of guilt.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb referring to a time immediately before the moment of speaking.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern Vた + ところだ describes an action completed just a moment ago.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the pattern Vたところです together with the adverb 今 to stress that B has just arrived, so A does not feel guilty about being late.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes something that happened recently from the speaker’s point of view. It may have happened a few weeks or months ago, so it does not mean that it finished just a moment ago like ところだ.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows an action in progress at the moment of speaking (being on the way), not an action that has already reached its destination.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse Vたところ (just finished doing something) with Vているところ (be doing something) and V辞書形ところ (be about to do something).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ところだ / ところです
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: An interrogative word combined with でも, giving an all-inclusive meaning in an affirmative sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: A group 2 verb changed into the potential form to show ability.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: Question word (何 / だれ / どこ / いつ / どれ) ＋ でも
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The topic is 青山さん. It combines 何でも with the potential-form predicate 食べられる to confirm that the character can eat food from the entire range without being picky.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It must be used with a negative predicate to express complete negation (not eat anything).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It refers to one unclear thing (eat something), and does not include everything like 何でも.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 何でも (anything—used with an affirmative statement) and 何も (nothing—must be used with a negative statement).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi:
A: “Has your summer vacation plan been decided?”
B: “Yes. I’m thinking of traveling.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase + の modifies and limits the following noun よてい.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the noun meaning “plan” the topic of the question.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb 決まる in the polite past tense + the particle か asks whether the state has been completed.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: A polite response word showing agreement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb する in the volitional form combines with the particle と to introduce an intention.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern V意向形 + と思っている describes an intention considered and held before the moment of speaking.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: Speaker B answers about a personal plan by combining the volitional form with と思っています to show an intention that was considered and developed before being asked.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows a decision or plan that is much firmer than the flexible intention expressed by と思っています.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It usually expresses an intention that has just arisen at the moment of speaking, rather than one considered beforehand.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Use と思っています when the intention has been considered beforehand. If only と思います is used, the sentence usually suggests a decision made suddenly while speaking.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と思っている / と思います
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi:
A: “Please write your name here.”
B: “Is it all right if I write it in Katakana?”
A: “Yes, that’s fine.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the destination or location where the result of the writing action is placed.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the object to be written.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vてください is used to make a polite request or give a polite instruction.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で shows the means or form used to write the characters.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: is it all right if I write it?”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vてもいいですか is used to ask permission to do an action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb 構う in the polite negative form, together with よ, shows that there is completely no problem with accepting something.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: Person B uses the permission-request pattern Vてもいいですか together with the particle で, which shows the method of writing, and person A replies with かまいません to show willing permission.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Shows an absolute prohibition, completely opposite to the permission meaning of てもいい.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Shows an obligation to do something, not a request for permission.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: The particle で in 「カタカナで」 shows the method, material, or language used to express something. Do not confuse it with the particles に or を.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: Sir/Madam, let me carry your luggage for you. Your room is this way.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: A polite term used to address a customer.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: A compound noun with the honorific prefix お- and the particle を, marking the object of the action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.vi: let me carry it for you.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The humble pattern お + V(stem) + します lowers the speaker when serving the other person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the noun with the prefix お- the topic for giving directions.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite directional pronoun こちら combines with the formal polite form でございます instead of です.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.cn: お + V(stem - group 1, 2) + します / いたします
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The staff use the humble pattern お〜します for their own actions to show humble service. They also use the highest honorific form でございます when showing the customer the location.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This is an honorific form used only for the customer's actions. Never use it for the speaker's own actions.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: It suggests doing someone a favor, so it is very rude when used with customers in service communication.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: The structure お + V(stem) + します is a humble form used only for the speaker's action toward the listener. It must not be used to talk about the other person's action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi:
(At home)
A: "Today, my teacher praised me at school!"
B: "Really? That's great!"
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place and setting where the conversation takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: A time word combined with the filler particle ね to attract the listener's attention.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the place where the praising action takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb ほめる is in the passive form and means positively receiving praise, followed by the particle よ.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: An interjection used to respond to information.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: A past-form adjective + the particle ね to share the other person's happiness and show empathy.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: V(group 1: aれる / group 2: られる / される / こられる)
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: Speaker A received the action of being praised, so A uses the passive form (ほめられた). The person who performed the praising action is 先生, marked by the particle に.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: The active sentence focuses on the teacher's action rather than the speaker's experience of being praised.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: It clearly emphasizes gratitude and appreciation for being praised by the teacher.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: In a Japanese passive sentence, the person who performs the action always takes the particle に, not が or を.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: You must not touch this computer.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase with the particle に, showing the object touched by the action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb さわる in the て form combines with the particle は to form the conditional clause leading to a prohibition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending forms the complete sentence pattern 〜てはいけません and expresses a formal prohibition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The verb さわる always takes the particle に to mark the object being touched. The structure Vてはいけません is used to give a firm but polite prohibition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 〜なくてもいいです means that something does not have to be done, or is not required. This is completely opposite to the strict prohibition expressed by 〜てはいけません.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 〜なければなりません shows that something must be done. It is the opposite of the prohibition against doing something expressed by 〜てはいけません.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle used with the verb さわる. They must use に for the object being touched, not the particle を.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi:
(At a friend's house)
A: "The dog keeps looking at us, doesn't it?"
B: "Yes, it wants to go outside and play, doesn't it?"
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase showing the setting where the conversation takes place, with the particle で.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The subject of the observed action, marked by the particle が in a sentence describing a visible situation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb modifying the sentence and showing that the action continues without stopping.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A directional pronoun combined with the particle を, showing the target of the looking action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 見る in the ている form describes an action happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: An interjection showing agreement with the previous statement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: A place noun with the particle に, showing the destination of the movement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.7.vi: it wants to go, doesn't it?"
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern V<s>たがる in the ている form describes the visible desire or wish of a third-person subject.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: Because the subject is a third-person subject, the dog, and the speaker observes outward signs of its behavior, the pattern 'V<s>たがる' in the 行きたがっている form must be used instead of the ending 'たい'.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: 〜たい is used only to directly express the speaker's own desire, in the first person, or to ask the listener directly. It is not used directly for a third person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 〜そうだ expresses a judgment based on outward appearance, such as "it looks like it wants to go," while 〜たがっている confirms a specific action that clearly shows the subject's desire.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often incorrectly use the ending 〜たい directly for a third person, as in the incorrect sentence 犬が外に行きたいです. The grammatically correct form is 〜たがっている.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: V<s> + たがる・たがっている
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: (At the station) A: "Good morning. Oh, aren't you taking the bus?" B: "Yes, I decided to walk to the office."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.sk: N(place) で + A: N に Vない + んですか + B: N まで V辞書形 + ことにする
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The setting where the conversation takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A greeting that opens the conversation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An interjection showing surprise when noticing something.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に used with the verb のる to show the vehicle someone gets on.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The sentence ending のんですか is used to ask for confirmation or ask for a reason based on the actual situation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: An affirmative reply to A's question.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle まで shows the destination of the movement.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with ことにする to turn the chosen action into a noun.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: The grammar pattern ことにした is used with んです to explain the reason to the other person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The pattern 「〜ことにする」 expresses the speaker's deliberate decision (walking instead of taking the bus). The verb before this pattern uses the dictionary form 「歩く」 to show that the action was chosen intentionally.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses an objective decision made because of circumstances or by a group, not the speaker's own will.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 「ことにする」 (deciding for oneself) with 「ことになる」 (an objective decision arranged by other people or circumstances).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ことにする
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: (At home) A: "You look unwell. Are you all right?" B: "Yes, I think I will sleep for a while. Wake me up at 3 o'clock."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.sk: A: N が Aい(remove い)そう + だけど + B: 時刻 に + Vたら + Vてね
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The physical setting of the conversation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ぐあい combines with the particle が to mark the subject expressing a physical condition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 悪い drops い and combines with そうだ to make an appearance-based guess, together with けど to connect the clauses.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending な appears at the end of a question asking the other person to confirm their condition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: A casual reply used in everyday communication.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb that modifies the degree of the action of sleeping.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The volitional form of the verb combines with かな to express an intention spoken to oneself.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle に marks a specific point in time.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb なる changes to the たら form to create a time condition for when that time arrives.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.9.n: The verb in the て form with ね is used to make a gentle, informal request.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい(remove い)かった・Aな/Nだった + ら
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The clause 「３時になったら」 uses the 「〜たら」 form to express a future time condition (when 3 o'clock arrives), leading to the request 「起こして」 in the following clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used only for an inevitable result and cannot be followed by a request, favor, or command.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It introduces a topic or an assumed situation. It is not used for a natural time point arriving, followed by a request as in this sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: After the assumed clauses 「〜と」 and 「〜ば」, a request or command (such as 起こしてね) cannot be used; 「〜たら」 must be used.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: My younger brother does nothing but play and refuses to do his homework.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vて + ばかりいる expresses an action that is repeated too much, with a complaining tone. It uses the て form to connect the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of doing.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative predicate shows that the task is not carried out.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The structure 「〜てばかりいる」 is used to criticize or complain about a negative habit repeated many times (playing all the time), which causes the person to neglect what they need to do (not doing homework).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply expresses the limit "only" and is neutral, without a complaining or negative feeling.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: The pattern 「〜てばかりいる」 always has a negative, complaining feeling. It is not used for positive or praiseworthy actions.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Vて形・N + ばかり（いる）
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: (At the library) A: "Excuse me, please do not eat or drink here." B: "Oh, I'm sorry."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.sk: N(place) では + N を + Vない + でください
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: States the place where the dialogue takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: A polite opening used to get someone's attention before giving a reminder.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The place word ここ combines with で to show the place of the action, and は emphasizes the area where it is forbidden.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of eating.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vないでください is used to politely ask or remind someone not to do something.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: An interjection showing that the speaker realizes a mistake after being reminded.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: An apology showing that the speaker accepts the reminder.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: To politely and appropriately ask or remind someone not to do something (eating or drinking in a public place), we use the structure 「〜ないでください」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a strict rule or prohibition and is less gentle and polite when reminding someone.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: A casual expression used between friends. It is not suitable for polite communication with others in a public place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: The verb must first be changed to the ない form and then joined with 「〜でください」. Do not confuse it with the て form.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: A: "Would you like to go see a movie or do something?" B: "Sounds good. Shall we go together?"
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.sk: A: N でも + V(remove ます) に + 行きませんか + B: V(remove ます) ましょうか
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle でも gives a representative example to make a gentle suggestion.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the ます form drops ます and combines with に to show the purpose of moving.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite negative sentence ending Vませんか is used to invite or suggest something to the other person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A phrase showing agreement with and support for the speaker's invitation.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The sentence ending Vましょうか is used to suggest doing an action together.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: The particle 「でも」 gives a typical suggestion (such as watching a movie) to invite the other person tactfully, implying that doing something else would also be fine. It is used with the purpose pattern 「V(remove ます) + に行く」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It directly identifies the only object as watching a movie, making the invitation more direct and less flexible.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: When used in an invitation, the particle でも means "such as..." or "for example," not the contrastive meaning "even though/but."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: This is the ring that my mother gave me.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.sk: N1 は ＋ N2(giver) が ＋ N3(receiver) に ＋ くれた ＋ N4 です
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative pronoun combined with the particle は states the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the receiver of the action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb くれる is changed into the short past form to modify the noun ゆびわ.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun combined with です forms a predicate that identifies the thing.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: N(giver) が ＋ N(receiver) に ＋ くれる
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The verb 「くれる」 describes an action in which another person gives something to the speaker themselves (わたし) or to someone in the speaker's family. The phrase 「母がわたしにくれた」 acts as an attributive modifier for the noun 「ゆびわ」.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Use it only when the speaker gives something to another person. Do not use it when another person gives something to the speaker.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: The subject must change to the receiver (わたしは母に...), meaning 'I received it from my mother'.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Never use 「あげる」 when another person gives something to the speaker or does something for the speaker.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: (At your friend's house) A: "This is delicious, isn't it? Could you show me how to make this salad?" B: "Sure."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の links a modifier to the following noun for a place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: An exclamatory opening that gives praise and leads into a request.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun for the salad.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の connects the noun for the food with the noun for the method of making it.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the object receiving the teaching action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern 〜てもらえますか is used to make a polite request to the other person.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: A cheerful response agreeing to the request.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます） ＋ 方（かた） / Vて ＋ もらえますか
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The speaker uses the phrase 『作り方』 to indicate the method of preparing the food, combined with the 『〜てもらえますか』 form to make a polite and tactful request.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It has a more familiar and less formal requesting tone than 〜てもらえますか.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a direct command meaning 'please show me,' without checking the other person's willingness.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: The rule for forming the noun meaning 'how to make something' 『〜かた』 requires removing ます (for example, つくりかた, not つくるかた).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: (At school) A: "Oh, where is Mr. Sato?" B: "He is not here now, but I think he will return in about 30 minutes."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase indicating the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: An interjection showing surprise or that something seems unusual.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は states the person being looked for and omits the predicate at the end of the question.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb indicating the present time.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle には emphasizes the place where the subject is currently absent.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The honorific form of います combined with the particle が connects two contrasting clauses.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb indicating the amount of time remaining before an action occurs.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle ほど indicates an estimated amount, combined with で to indicate the completion point.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: The honorific structure 『お＋Vますremove ます＋になる』 honors the teacher's action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: The pattern と思います expresses the speaker's subjective judgment or opinion.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: お ＋ Vます（remove ます） ＋ になる / 普通形 ＋ と思う
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the two honorific forms 『いらっしゃいません』 and 『おもどりになる』 together to show respect for Mr. Sato, and combines them with 『〜と思います』 to give a polite judgment.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This is only the regular polite form and does not show respect for the teacher.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a humble form used only for oneself, so using it for the teacher is an incorrect honorific choice.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the honorific pattern 『お〜になる』 (for someone of higher status) with the humble form 『お〜する』 (lowering oneself).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: The room I am living in now is both expensive and cramped, so I want to move.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of time modifying the action of living.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The ている form of the verb creates an attributive clause modifying the room.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は identifies the topic to be evaluated and explained.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle し lists the first reason.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The conjunction ので states the objective reason leading to the wish in the following clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The ending 〜たいです expresses the desire to move to a new place to live.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: 普通形 ＋ し / 普通形（Aな・N な） ＋ ので / Vます（remove ます） ＋ たい
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The sentence uses 『〜し』 to list several negative reasons in parallel and ends with 『〜ので』 to give a reasonable explanation for the wish to move in the main clause.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply connects two adjectives and does not emphasize the listing of several reasons as し does.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Repeating から sounds awkward and makes the sentence seem overly subjective.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Before 『し』 and 『ので』, an adjective ending in い keeps the ending い instead of removing い.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: Every morning, I try to keep walking for one hour.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of time showing a regular cycle.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A quantity phrase indicating how long the action lasts.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies ように to identify the goal of the action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.vi: I always try to maintain it.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜ようにしている describes making an effort to maintain a good daily habit.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The structure 『〜ようにしている』 combined with the frequency adverb 『毎朝』 clearly shows the speaker's self-discipline and effort to make walking a regular daily habit.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It indicates that the matter was decided by outside circumstances or another person, not by the speaker's own effort.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes a change of state over time rather than emphasizing the effort to maintain a habit.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish 『〜ようにする』 (actively making an effort to form a habit) from 『〜ようになる』 (a natural change of state).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようにする / ようにしている
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: A: "May I use the computer?" B: "No, do not use the computer. Write with a pen instead."
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を indicates the object affected by the action of using.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb changed into the て form combines with も to create a permission-request condition.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜てもいいですか is used to ask the other person for permission.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A word used to deny and refuse the request for permission.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes the noun the topic and contrasts it with the tool used afterward.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The V-ずに pattern describes not doing one action and doing another instead.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle で indicates the tool or means used to write.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern 〜てください is used to make a polite request or instruction.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もいいですか / Vない（remove ない） ＋ ずに（※ する → せずに）
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: After refusing the permission request 『〜てもいいですか』, speaker B uses the pattern 『〜ずに』 (equivalent to 〜ないで) to tell speaker A not to do this action but to replace it with another action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the same meaning but is more conversational and more common in daily communication than ずに.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used to express a reason (because one does not use it...), not an accompanying state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: A group 3 verb changes with ずに in the special form 『せずに』, not 『しずに』.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: As for vegetables, they are cheaper at the supermarket over there.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that vegetables are the topic being compared.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あっち with the noun スーパー, creating the meaning 'the supermarket over there.'
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects スーパー with ほう and indicates the side or choice used for comparison.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうが marks the side considered to have the higher degree in the comparison.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 安い is the い adjective serving as the predicate, while です makes the expression polite.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: State the object being compared with は, then use N2 のほうが to indicate the side with the stronger characteristic. The adjective 安い comes at the end to conclude the statement about the price.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If より is added after N1, the meaning becomes clearer: N2 is cheaper than N1.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 同じくらい, the meaning changes to say that the two sides are equal in degree.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse は and が, but in this comparison pattern は states the topic, while が marks the side rated higher.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.cn: N1 は ＋ N2 のほうが ＋ Aいです／Nです
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Distance ＋ Vて ＋ います
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase placed at the beginning of the sentence to show when the action takes place.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A quantity phrase indicating the distance covered by the running action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of はしる connects the verb with います in the Vている pattern.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the Vている pattern and describes a continued action or repeated habit.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The time and distance phrases come before the verb to add the circumstances and extent of the action. The はしって form combines with います to describe running regularly every morning.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If はしります is used, the sentence only states a habit or general fact and does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If はしってから is used, it means that another action happens after running, so the sentence is incomplete when used alone.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may mechanically translate Vている as 'be doing,' but with a repeated habit such as this sentence, it can mean maintaining the action regularly.
